summary: The note presents ten practices for sourcing meat ethically while honoring regional culinary traditions, from knowing your farmer and reading welfare labels to choosing heritage breeds, regenerative agriculture, less popular cuts, seasonal eating, CSAs and flexitarian eating. Each practice is paired with an example dish and a named expert, author or event. The conclusion frames the modern cook as a custodian of tradition and an advocate for ethical animal husbandry.
one_line: Ten practical ways to source and eat meat ethically while preserving regional recipes, each tied to a dish and a named expert.
key_facts: Chef Juliana Lopez, starting September 5, 2023, promotes the local food movement, saying "You have to shake the hand that feeds you."

Sam Richardson, a rancher and humane-treatment advocate, said at a conference on October 16, 2023 that Animal Welfare Approved, Certified Humane, and Global Animal Partnership labels imply strict welfare standards.
As of November 22, 2023, chef and restaurateur Michael Ford has championed heritage breeds, saying "They aren't just unique flavors; they are storytelling."
Dr. Anna Zimmerman, a Boston-based agricultural expert, published work on September 10, 2023 stating "Livestock plays a vital role in regenerative systems."
Chef Luis Gomez used less traditional cuts at a pop-up event on December 1, 2023, saying "The oxtail stew is not just a comfort dish; it's a statement."
Dietitian Emily Thompson, interviewed January 15, 2024, said seasonal eating "aligns our diets with the natural growth and breeding cycles."
On September 1, 2023, a study from the University of Ethical Farming found that a plant-fed diet for livestock results in happier and healthier animals.
Food writer Rachel Anderson praised CSA programs in an October article for bringing transparency and community engagement to meat sourcing.
The documentary "Carnivore's Dilemma" was released on November 30, 2023 and is recommended for understanding the meat industry.
Dr. Lila Greene's book "The Part-Time Carnivore" was released October 5, 2023 and recommends smaller meat portions, boosting the flexitarian diet.
Rotational grazing for cattle is cited as a way to improve soil health and biodiversity, linked to the beef bourguignon example.
The note advises avoiding meat from animals fed animal byproducts, linking these to inhumane and environmentally damaging practices.
